description: A sourced guide to SBA-backed financing for a small business, ranked for the owner's need: 7(a) small, Standard 7(a), SBA Express, 504, Microloan, the export loans (Export Express, Export Working Capital, International Trade) and the disaster loans (physical damage and EIDL). Give any of amount_needed, purposes, years_in_business and state. Each fitting program comes with why it fits, what it is for, its maximum amount, terms, SBA's published interest-rate maximums where SBA sets them, key requirements, who makes the loan, how to apply and its official sba.gov page; programs that do not fit say why. Then the next steps: SBA Lender Match and free or low-cost counseling from SBDCs, SCORE, Women's Business Centers and Veterans Business Outreach Centers, with locator links for the state when given. Facts are from sba.gov as of 2026-11-03, returned in as_of. Use it when a for-profit small business finds few grants it qualifies for. Static reference with no network access. Informational, not financial advice.

purposes.description: Every use that applies: working_capital, equipment, real_estate, buy_a_business, startup, inventory, refinance_debt, export, disaster_recovery.

state.description: Two-letter code for a U.S. state, DC, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa or the Northern Mariana Islands, for example MT.

years_in_business.description: Years the business has operated. 0 if it has not opened yet.

name: sba_loans
title: SBA loans that fit
